18: If MODFLOW does not converge on the first day, try the COMPLEX solver and read the group FAQ; if it still fails, send the MODFLOW file.
17: A model that runs a single period may still be set to steady state: change SS to TR (transient) in the .dis file.
52: When a DEM upload fails, check first that the DEM is a TIFF; if it still fails, the project is needed.
53: A MODFLOW domain smaller than the catchment is allowed: there is no exchange where the models do not overlap, and SWAT groundwater still runs. Running SWAT alone shows whether the crash comes from the coupling.
13: MODFLOW steps that differ from the coupled run do not look like an error. The useful question is whether the model crashes, and the files show it.
35: When runoff differs between SWAT and SWAT-MODFLOW-RT3D, calibrate in order: lower K and Sy, raise CN2, then the river parameters.
19: The units of the observed values in RVOB must be consistent with the model.
8: Outputs that can feed a flood model exist at HRU, subbasin and grid scales; the question is which scale you need.
22: All SWAT percolation goes to MODFLOW as recharge; to reduce it, adjust CN, ET and the soil parameters.
39: To lower a simulated groundwater level by about 10 m, look at K, Sy, layer thicknesses, boundaries and initial heads.
20: Monthly calibration is fine for a snow-dominated basin; stress periods follow pumping, and recharge comes from SWAT.
24: The recharge output is derived from SWAT percolation; the approach is reasonable, but check the water balance.
40: Ask one clear question at a time: a reply can answer only what it understands.
27: A grid-reading error such as UnboundLocalError (delr) means the plug-in could not read the grid rows; the .dis file shows why.
44: A missing output file such as swatmf_out_MF_obs usually means the model crashed before writing it.
4: Before plotting, check that the simulation actually ran.
30: If the run button does nothing, first ask whether the linking succeeded; the error messages and the .lst file tell.
55: An irrigation file full of zeros cannot be diagnosed from the text: the project folder and GIS file are needed.
6: For the MODFLOW discretization file, use ModelMuse; the tutorials explain it.
21: To export the MODFLOW grid shapefile, use the ModelMuse menu; the attributes are not needed.
15: QSWATMOD needs a defined list of inputs, and the documentation lists them.
0: A TypeError when exporting modflow.obs was fixed in v2.3.1: check that the latest version is installed.
12: Duplicated lines in the yearly exchange output depend on the number of river cells and on the simulation period, warm-up included.
5: Odd water-table elevations compared with ModelMuse call for the MODFLOW model settings and parameter values.
32: There is no known limit to the number of wells in MODFLOW.
37: Cyclical discharge in some subbasins: look at the tolerance settings in the .nwt file and at the head elevation, and check the water table.
47: SWAT and MODFLOW may use different time steps and periods: that is allowed, and the MODFLOW model can be extended with dummy years.
11: A MODFLOW model has to exist before the coupling steps; for several layers, build it in ModelMuse.
45: If adding the well package fails, create the well package first (QSWATMOD cannot make it): use ModelMuse.
42: If only a few cells show exchange and the recharge looks odd, the problem may be in the mf_grid layer; the group has a link on adding or subtracting rows and columns.
48: When SWAT and MODFLOW cover different numbers of years, the run ends at the earlier end date: extend the MODFLOW model.
10: A “file not found” error on unit 146 can come from the solver: if it is PCG and not NWT, try NWT.
23: The tool builds a single layer: for several layers, use ModelMuse.
43: The timing of irrigation from pumping is not a code change: use the .mgt schedule or the MODFLOW settings.
50: An end-of-file error on the well file at period 2 can mean the MODFLOW period is too short: add about 100 days to it (leap years).
26: A TypeError when exporting modflow.obs was fixed in version 2.3.1: upgrade.
9: For an ArcSWAT-MODFLOW project, use QSWATMOD instead of SWATMOD-prep; the group has a link.
